headline: Genome-scale and hybrid models reconstruct microbial metabolism and community dynamics
label: Metabolic Network Modeling Methods
summary: May 2026 preprints extend genome-scale metabolic models to enzyme annotation, microbiome dynamics, and membrane transport prediction.
synthesis: The dominant thread is genome-scale metabolic modeling extended beyond single-organism reconstruction. MetaGEM builds models bottom-up by predicting enzyme-metabolite interactions with a dual-tower protein language model and 3D metabolite representations. DySCoMeMo couples ecological dynamical systems models with constraint-based metabolic models to forecast host-microbiome dynamics. A seven-member maize root synthetic community, modeled in exudate medium, predicts cross-feeding and identifies Enterobacter ludwigii as a community hub. CFCMM consolidates 13 fungal models into a ModelSEED-consistent template and uses flux balance analysis to predict ATP yields. A feature-learning coarse-graining approach identifies conserved cross-species growth predictors. ChemProFlow is less directly constraint-based: it applies geometric deep learning to predict molecular transportability, assigns TCDB transport mechanisms, and maps these to microorganisms. The new element is integration of reconstruction, community dynamics, and learned molecular or protein representations within metabolic modeling workflows.
